title: Galleon (USA).xiso.iso
prediction: THE COST SIDE of #44's skew bound, on its own request because a pgraph disc emits no usable gfps and the accuracy request cannot price it. Arm A is the instrument with the bound compiled off; arm B is XEMU_OPT_FIFO_SKEW_BOUND 0 -> 1 and nothing else. Both Galleon, 240 s, --device nova, one requester, device_label read out of each result.json. WHAT IS BEING PRICED: every submission the guest makes becomes a round trip to the PFIFO thread where before it was a store that returned immediately. frame-pacing-and-parallelism.md measured the guest CPU thread busy 83% of the wall clock on this class of scene, the renderer idle 21.2 ms of a 50.2 ms frame waiting on it, and the guest blocked on the renderer for the other 8.7 ms -- so the two halves were already only partly overlapped and this removes what overlap remains. It could be small or it could be a third of the frame rate; nothing in the tree says which, which is why this is a measurement and not an estimate. C0 (THE SIZE OF THE THING BEING PRICED, arm A alone, and it is the number this whole lane was missing): report kicks/s, the pushbuffer ring limit in bytes, the share of submissions made with PGRAPH behind, and the publish-to-consumed skew distribution. No threshold: nothing has ever measured any of them, so a registered bound would be a guess dressed as a prediction. It is recorded as a survey, not counted as a leg. C1 (THE COST, on the CEILING and never the median): gfps p90 and gfps max each fall by no more than 2 from arm A to arm B. The statistic is declared here in advance because #64 measured the median on this queue to be a measurement of device occupancy -- bimodal, ceiling 29-31 and floor 5-20, moving 80% to 16-32% across one evening while p90 stayed 29/29/27/29 and max 31/29/30/29 over four runs, two refs, both orders -- and #65's U6 went median 33 -> 29 on a change that did not move the ceiling at all. FAILS at a fall of 3 or more on either, and then the bound as written is too expensive to ship on by default and the trade goes back to the device owner with both numbers, per orchestration.md: measure the accuracy, then the cost, then hand it over rather than resolving it. C2 (DID IT EXECUTE): arm B's held(n) is at least 90% of its kicks. A cost leg on an inert change is worthless, and a flat gfps cannot distinguish the two. FAILS if held(n) is near zero, and then the DMA_PUT-advanced gate in pfifo_kick never fired on this title either and C1 measured nothing. C3 (WHERE THE COST GOES, so a failure of C1 has a direction): report spun/slept. The 60 us spin exists because the pusher already spins 100 us before parking, so a submission consumed while it is awake costs neither thread a futex. If slept dominates, the cost is scheduler round trips and the spin window is the thing to change; if spun dominates and C1 still fails, the cost is the serialisation itself and no spin tuning reaches it. Recorded as a diagnosis, not counted as a leg. C4 (must-not-move, the sanity check that the bound has not broken pacing outright): whole-soak VBLANK delivered rate from the vbl line stays within 0.5 Hz between arms. The bound does not touch the VBLANK grid, and Galleon reports Ul:N throughout so neither the deferral cap change below it nor this can reach the unlock branch. FAILS if the rate moves more, and then holding the guest at its submission point is perturbing the timebase as well as the frame rate, which is a second effect and would need its own arm. C5 (THE HOLE, on a title rather than a test disc): gave, the count of releases with pushbuffer still outstanding, is reported as a RATE per submission rather than as a pass or a fail. Galleon flips every frame, so unlike #44's eighteen-draws-in-one-frame disc it exercises FLIP_STALL constantly, and the guarantee genuinely does not hold across a flip stall -- the alternative is a deadlock. A high rate here does not falsify the fix for #44; it bounds how much of a real title's submissions the bound actually covers, which is the honest scope of the change and is currently unknown.

note_refs: a_ref 90c5b88033 is the instrument with the bound compiled off; b_ref 008298446d is that plus XEMU_OPT_FIFO_SKEW_BOUND 0 -> 1. Both are descendants of e62907fa03 (the unlock defer_cap change), which is therefore constant across this pair and cannot confound it. Galleon never enters unlock mode (Ul:N on all 129 windows of both of #65's arms), so that change is inert on this title in any case. A soak writes no captures, so ab_compare cannot score it and this file is bound by being committed before either arm was queued.
